expectations.text: Assesses all ten GENSEC best practices by ID (GENSEC01-BP01..BP04, GENSEC02-BP01, GENSEC03-BP01, GENSEC04-BP01, GENSEC04-BP02, GENSEC05-BP01, GENSEC06-BP01)
expectations.evidence: The 'Full assessment' table has exactly ten rows, one per GENSEC practice, each with Status / Lens risk / Adjusted risk / Evidence. Script-verified: the set of GENSEC IDs in the output equals the set of ten GENSEC IDs in assets/best-practices.csv. Seven of the ten also get a developed priority finding; the remaining three (GENSEC01-BP01, GENSEC05-BP01, GENSEC06-BP01) are assessed in the table plus the exclusions section.

expectations.text: Every GEN*-BP* ID cited actually exists in the Lens — no fabricated IDs
expectations.evidence: Verified with a script against assets/best-practices.csv. outputs/response.md cites 13 distinct IDs (the ten GENSEC plus GENOPS01-BP02, GENOPS03-BP01, GENOPS03-BP02 flagged as security-adjacent out-of-scope items); all 13 matched the authoritative list. Fabricated set empty.

expectations.text: Addresses prompt injection through GENSEC04-BP02 and data leakage through GENSEC01-BP03
expectations.evidence: Finding 1 is 'GENSEC01-BP03 — Implement least privilege access permissions for foundation models accessing data stores ... This is your data leakage finding'. Finding 2 is 'GENSEC04-BP02 — Sanitize and validate user inputs to foundation models', which separates direct injection ('Impact is genuinely limited in this workload: no tools means no actions') from indirect injection via retrieved Confluence content ('this is the real finding ... A single line of white text or an HTML comment on an obscure page ... becomes a company-wide misinformation and phishing channel') and names the markdown-image exfiltration variant.

expectations.text: Adjusts at least one practice's risk rating away from the Lens's inherent rating because the workload is internal and SSO-gated, and justifies the adjustment
expectations.evidence: Finding 5, GENSEC01-BP02: '**Risk:** Medium (Lens: High)' with the justification 'It's TLS-encrypted, so this is a defence-in-depth gap rather than an active exposure — which is why I've lowered it from the Lens's inherent High. The workload is internal, SSO-gated, and has no external caller to attract attention.' The full-assessment table records the same in a dedicated 'Adjusted' column ('Lowered: TLS in transit, internal workload, no external caller'), and GENSEC01-BP01 is likewise lowered High→Medium with 'Internal-only use lowers this.' Adjustments run both ways: GENSEC01-BP03 is raised High→Critical with a stated rationale.

expectations.text: Flags at least one practice as needing evidence the user hasn't supplied instead of guessing a verdict
expectations.evidence: 'Insufficient evidence' is used as a first-class status, not a caveat. GENSEC01-BP02: 'Status: Insufficient evidence ... Evidence: Network path not described.' GENSEC01-BP04: 'Status: Insufficient evidence — assume not met' with the reasoning stated ('Bedrock model invocation logging is off by default, so absent evidence to the contrary the safe assumption for a sign-off document is that it isn't on'). The 'Assessment at a glance' table carries a dedicated 'Insufficient evidence' column (count 2), and the closing note says these 'need a configuration check rather than new engineering, and several may already be met.'

expectations.text: Notes that GENSEC05-BP01 (excessive agency) is not applicable or low relevance for a read-only search bot, with justification
expectations.evidence: Table row: 'GENSEC05-BP01 | Least privilege for agentic workflows | N/A | High | — | No agent, no tool use, no actions. Re-open the moment anything is added.' Expanded in exclusions: '**GENSEC05-BP01 (excessive agency) — not applicable today, and fragile.** The bot answers; it does not act. But this is the practice that flips the severity of finding #2 from "misinformation" to "remote code execution by Confluence page" ... Recommend a written gate: no tool or action capability ships until GENSEC04-BP02 and GENSEC05-BP01 are both assessed as met.' Justification is present and the conditionality is made a sign-off condition.

claims.claim: The user asked for security only, so the other 41 practices are out of scope
claims.evidence: Arithmetic checks out: 51 total practices in best-practices.csv minus 10 GENSEC = 41. The scope warning is placed at the top ('A clean GENSEC review is not a clean Well-Architected review') and three security-adjacent non-GENSEC practices are named rather than silently dropped.

claims.claim: Confluence exports carry no ACL metadata, so Bedrock Knowledge Bases cannot infer space or page restrictions
claims.evidence: Accurate for a static space export ingested to S3. The run explicitly labels this its most load-bearing assumption (Assumption 1) and states what would change if the Kendra GenAI Index or the native Confluence connector were in use — appropriate hedging for an assessment made without repo access.

claims.claim: Enabling Bedrock invocation logging creates a second, more broadly readable copy of the sensitive corpus
claims.evidence: Correct and non-obvious: invocation logs contain full prompts including retrieved chunks, and central logging buckets typically have broader access than the source spaces. Both runs independently identify this; it is a genuine strength no assertion covers.

claims.claim: GENSEC06-BP01 is N/A as written but the underlying risk transfers to the RAG ingestion pipeline
claims.evidence: Defensible: the practice is scoped to training/customization workflows in best-practices.csv ('Implement data purification filters for model training workflows'), and the run scores it N/A 'to stay faithful to the Lens' while folding the ingestion-sanitization mitigation into finding #2 rather than losing it.

claims.claim: Four of the six High-risk GENSEC practices that apply are not met
claims.evidence: Consistent with the full-assessment table: of the eight applicable practices, those rated Lens-High and marked Not met are GENSEC01-BP03, GENSEC02-BP01, GENSEC04-BP02, plus GENSEC01-BP04 (Insufficient evidence — assume not met). Roll-up counts (0 met / 2 partial / 4 not met / 2 insufficient / 2 N/A = 10) reconcile with the table.

suggestions.reason: This is the eval where the baseline is genuinely competitive — it also assessed all ten GENSEC practices by correct ID (it web-searched the Lens docs; see its §9 Sources). The assertions that separate the two runs here are the 'insufficient evidence' and risk-adjustment ones, which is the right signal, but the eval would be sharper with an assertion about scope discipline: this run opens with a scope warning that a GENSEC-only pass is not a Well-Architected pass and names the 41 unassessed practices, which is a real reviewer behaviour nothing currently tests.

suggestions.assertion: Adjusts at least one practice's risk rating away from the Lens's inherent rating because the workload is internal and SSO-gated, and justifies the adjustment
suggestions.reason: 'Away from' is directionless, so an upward adjustment justified by the same context also satisfies it. If the intent is specifically that internal+SSO should *lower* something (testing that the reviewer doesn't just parrot Lens ratings upward), say 'lowers'.

eval_feedback.overall: Well-targeted assertions for a scoped single-pillar request; the 'insufficient evidence' assertion is the most discriminating one in the whole suite.
